_note: Деталь 4 — PEEK Radome v2c (02_01 §5.2 + 01_04 §5.5). Hollow PEEK dome Ø29.8 (= Zone-3 flange) — DERIVED from the board-contour target since the ROOT verdict (⚖️ founder 2026-09-29, applied 2026-09-30; 02_01 §3.5: target Ø19.97 + 2×0.2 collar (0.2 = the SLM print-floor default, the ground since 2026-10-01 - model 73, 02_02 4.4; the CNC route states no floor) + 2×4.715 rim boss), the Ø25 freeze is history. Wall 1.5-2.0 (RF vs strength). Cavity for PCB stack. NB cavity height is NOT antenna<->Ti clearance (that is cavityH - lockGrooveZ - t/2 = 8.0 at the bayonet datum) and the >=12 floor is OURS, not canon's (02_01 5.3 asks >=8) - 00_07 HW.33. Internal axial headroom is cavityH + inner cap radius, not cavityH. Shield bell >=3mm rise / R>=5 (anti-overgrowth, no callus edge). Bayonet socket = L-slot mating Деталь-3 lugs, cut in the OUTER band of a local internal RIM BOSS whose INNER band is the seal land; the rim is FLAT and the single O-ring groove is the flange's (00_07 HW.33 branch (а), applied 2026-09-14). The rim cavity under the boss, <=Ø20.37 at the 80 % gland fill (kept at 80 % — ⚖️ delegated 2026-09-30, 02_02 §3.2), is the CEILING handed to the board layout HW.9 as an input (every term a minimum). Vent facet + BME280 pocket (⚖️ 2026-09-29, 02_01 §3.4) applied 2026-09-30 — the vent_*/pocket_* fields; the geometry answers the verdict's conditional: VE70205 (ring 6.5) fits the facet, VE70308 (9.1) does not. Cathode O2 = side/perimeter (02_02 §1.2), NOT sealed under the dome.
name: radome

notes.material: PEEK (polyetheretherketone). The grade CLASS is not the requirement - an industrial or a medical grade is equally admissible and is judged by the properties named here and in surface_finish (delegated verdict 2026-09-29, 02_01 5.2); state the pigment and additive chemistry of the grade you use. Chosen for RF, not for strength: er 3.2 and tan d 0.003 at 868 MHz make it effectively transparent to the antenna, where water (er about 80) is the thing that is not (02_01 5.2). Canon names UV-stable PC/ASA as a declared alternative, under the same alpha <= 0.5 (a bark tone only with an NIR-reflective pigment - see surface_finish). Not a bio-contact part - but NOT mechanically idle either: 02_01 5.2 calls it an anti-vandal sealed cover, and 00_07 HW.33 makes its RIM a hard datum that lands on the flange top face and closes the single O-ring groove there, so treat the rim as a load-bearing sealing face
notes.process: Thermal moulding (термолиття) is the route costed in 02_06 1.2 at the 1K tier; the rim, however, is a machined DATUM face: under branch (а) of 00_07 HW.33 - with the bayonet clamping the rim onto the flange face (02_02 3.5 states the initial clamp) - the seal squeeze is set by the flange groove depth alone, and the FLATNESS of this rim is one of the two mating faces the +/-98 um O-ring chain must also cover (script 52 names it as a missing datum). No supplier is fixed. If your route differs, say so - the rim flatness is what the seal depends on, so the forming route is not a free choice here. ATTENTION (2026-09-30): the rim boss and the BME280 pocket housing are INTERNAL UNDERCUTS for a plain core - say whether your route uses a collapsible or split core, or machines them after forming; neither this manifest nor canon fixes that
notes.post_process: Thermal moulding needs no metallurgical post-process; the only post-forming operation canon names for this part is the machined FLAT RIM face that the O-ring chain depends on (00_07 HW.33) - the rim carries NO groove. If your route needs annealing or stress relief before that cut, say so - PEEK stress released after machining would drift exactly the seal datum
notes.surface_finish: SPECIFIED AS SOLAR ABSORPTANCE, NOT COLOUR: alpha <= 0.5 for the outer shell (delegated verdict 2026-09-27, 02_01 5.2; basis script 71 of 00_07 HW.37 - in full sun a dark shell (alpha 0.95) leaves the EDLC 2.0-5.7 K to its 70 C rating, a light one >= 15 K — re-run 2026-09-30 on the O29.8 dome; 3.6-7.1 / >= 16 on O25). Light means a UV-stable pigment (TiO2). Whether unpigmented PEEK darkens in sun is not sourced on our side; an alpha rise with age is not excluded either (02_01 5.2). A muted or bark tone (e.g. RAL 8007) is admissible ONLY with an NIR-reflective (cool) pigment and a MEASURED alpha <= 0.5 - an ordinary brown pigment is out. alpha <= 0.5 holds over the WHOLE service life, not only as delivered (delegated verdict 2026-10-01, 02_01 5.2: the verdict's ground is the hottest hour of 30 years, i.e. the service envelope): acceptance is a measured alpha after accelerated weathering (e.g. xenon-arc, ISO 4892-2) or a measured as-delivered alpha with a margin for aging - method, hours and margin follow the material supplier's ageing data. Say whether your alpha holds after UV aging, not only as delivered. State the grade and its measured alpha; the pigment also shifts er and tan-delta, so the RF check under the radome follows it (00_07 HW.17). The shell is the outward face of a device that sits on living bark for two decades, and 01_04 5.5 asks for a rounded top edge so callus cannot get a grip. The RIM is the exception - it is a sealing datum, not decoration (00_07 HW.33)
notes.coating_restriction: Nothing is applied to PEEK - 01_02 3.6 excludes ZnO-Ta, self-healing 8-HQ and biomimetic layers from PEEK surfaces outright. Beyond that map: any metallic or otherwise conductive coating, paint or label would defeat the single function this part exists for, since the antenna radiates THROUGH it (02_01 5.2). Consequence, not a canon clause - but it is the one that costs the link budget
notes.inspection: Wall thickness within the 1.5-2.0 mm band (02_01 5.2). ATTENTION: that band is an RF DESIGN band whose VNA validation has not been run (00_07 UNI.10), so it is a requirement to hold, not a measured margin to spend. ATTENTION 2: all three founder verdicts of 00_07 HW.33 are now APPLIED. (b) the rim is FLAT against a SINGLE 1.344 mm groove in the flange and (c) a local internal rim BOSS carries the bayonet socket in its outer band and the seal land in its inner band (rim cavity <=Ø20.37 at the 80 % gland fill - a CEILING for the board, every term a minimum, handed to HW.9 as an input; <=Ø15.57 on the Ø25 dome until the root, 2026-09-30) landed 2026-09-14; (a) the FLAT CROWN with an R5 edge round landed 2026-09-22, once the piezo-placement verdict HW.30 put the pad BESIDE the piezo and so left the board stack under the 16.0 mm the crown fixes (the piezo and its pad were cut on 2026-09-29, HW.30; the crown stays as ratified). Measured on the shipped geometry: outer height 18.0 mm over the rim, crown rise 5.0, internal height 16.0 = cavity 13.0 + inner round 3.0; Ø29.8 since 2026-09-30 (root: the dome grew for the board, the heights did not move). ATTENTION 3, and it is the one that would still scrap a batch: this manifest is STILL not an acceptance geometry, for a different reason - the raised COLLAR (02_02 4.4) is not modelled on either part, so the bayonet Z is un-reconciled and the socket here keeps a shape the collar leg will reshape. Do not cut a part from this manifest until that leg lands
extra: Деталь 4 of the mechanical stack; bayonet 1/4-turn onto Деталь 3 (the cathode flange), NEVER onto the Zone-1 gyroid anode - that mistake destroys the enzyme surface (02_01 5.2)
The cathode breathes O2 from the SIDE/perimeter under the bell, not from under this dome (01_04 5.5; 02_02 1.2 only cross-refs it) - the dome is not a gas reservoir

NO factory drawing exists for this part, and that is a RATIFIED DEFERRAL rather than a gap (00_07 HW.1). The crown half of the deferral is SPENT since 2026-09-22 - the cap is now the ratified flat crown - but the deferral stands on TWO other grounds: (1) the socket is reshaped by the collar leg (02_02 4.4, 00_07 HW.33), so a sheet issued today would print a socket that is about to change; (2) the BME280 pocket floor pocket_floor_over_rim_mm is a PLACEHOLDER (the RF-deck top, moved by the B2B / rigid-flex pair height, 00_07 HW.29), and a sheet would print it as a decision. Draw it with the LAST of those changes, never before. A form NOT chosen: print the pocket floor as loud absence (NOT SPECIFIED IN CEM), which would leave the collar the only ground. Until then these notes are the SOURCE of the acceptance contract and have no carrier

The raised COLLAR that carries the flange lugs at Assembly.RequiredLugZMm (02_02 4.4, ratified 2026-09-11) is not modelled on either part. Strength does not size its wall (model 73, 02_02 4.4, 2026-10-01: lug-root shear carries 457 N already at 0.2; there is still no bayonet load model, but the force no longer sizes the wall) - the process floor does (SLM route: the vendor's slm_min_wall_mm, default 0.2, 01_01 5.5; CNC route: the shop's minimum standing wall, not stated); confined ice is held by no wall that fits the socket band, only drainage (FMEA #26). What holds the collar now is its running clearance in the radome channel: any non-zero clearance moves the root, and whether the collar needs one nothing states (52 collar_radial_budget; 00_07 HW.9, held under the crown pause). The socket here keeps its L-slot shape clipped to the outer band of the boss until that leg reshapes it - socket and collar are the female and male halves of one band (00_07 HW.33)

VENT + SENSOR POCKET (2026-09-30; verdict 2026-09-29, 02_01 3.4; numbers radome_vent_shortlist): a flat inward PAD on the vertical inner wall at 60 deg (between two entry slots), 8.5 wide, carrying a raised Gore target ring ID 6.5 x 0.5 high for a VE70205 (glued INSIDE; a 9.1 ring for VE70308 does NOT fit this dome - the verdict said which, the geometry answered) and ONE through-hole O1.0 to the outside. The BME280 pocket = a duct standing on the boss top outside the rim cavity + a chamber over the RF-deck edge inside it + a bridge above the board edge, about 90 mm3 of air sealed from the capsule - the chamber is OPEN at the bottom onto the board and its rim is a gasket land the board layout must provide (HW.9; the gasket is not a part in any BOM yet). Its floor, 11.85 over the rim, is a PLACEHOLDER (RF-deck top at FR4 1.6 + B2B 8; HW.29 / HW.9 move it). PEEK under the adhesive ring: plasma to >= 55 mN/m, dyne-pen check, glue and cure BEFORE the sensor enters the capsule (shortlist 2.6). No supplier has qualified silicone PSA on treated PEEK for 20 years - the bench decides (00_07 HW.32)
